## CDA ANOVAs

If second assumption fails, use welsh's t-test which is the default for t.test function regardless.

Assumptions of welsh t-test: a) normality of data, b) homoscedasticity (variance of two samples equal)

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(broom)

#read in data
setwd("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/McGill/Soper Lab/AusStoich")
aus_data <- read_csv(file = "Inputs/aus_data2026.csv")

#save results in one tibble after each test:
test_results <- tibble()
```

## putative_BNF

Since it only has two levels, use t.test.

### ln_leaf_N

```{r}
#check normality assumption
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF ==1)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N BNF 1")
hist(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF ==0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N BNF 0")

qqnorm(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF == 1)$ln_leaf_N, main ="leaf N 1")
qqline(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF == 1)$ln_leaf_N, col = "red")

qqnorm(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF == 0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N 0")
qqline(filter(aus_data, putative_BNF == 0)$ln_leaf_N, col = "red")

#check assumption of equal variance
var.test(ln_leaf_N ~ putative_BNF, data = aus_data) 
bartlett.test(ln_leaf_N ~ putative_BNF, data = aus_data)
leveneTest(ln_leaf_N ~ factor(putative_BNF), data = aus_data)

#do test
BNF_leafN_t_test <- t.test(data = aus_data, ln_leaf_N ~ putative_BNF, var.equal = FALSE)

print(BNF_leafN_t_test)
```

Variances unequal, so use welsh specifically with var.equal = FALSE. Significant difference.

Save test using tidy:

```{r}
test_results <- BNF_leafN_t_test %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  mutate(test_source = "BNF_leaf_N") %>% 
  bind_rows(test_results, . )
```

## myc_type

Assumptions of ANOVA: a) normality of data (+ residuals), b) homoscedasticity, c) additivity

a\) can assess using residuals of ANOVA model in a wwplot.

b\) verify using residuals vs. fitted plot or scale-location plot - should have equivalent spread of residuals for each of the fitted values.or perform bartlett.test (p values should be \> 0.05 for homoscedasticity to be respected)

c\) consider whether effects of two factors are additive: if the effect of one factor remains constant over all levels of the other factor, and that each factor influences the response independently of the other factor

We are going to assume the combined mycorrhizal types are independent of their component parts, due to ecological reasons.

First, assess normality of data for all 6 leaf traits.

```{r}
nutrients <- c("ln_leaf_N", "ln_leaf_P", "leaf_C_per_dry_mass",
               "ln_NP_ratio", "ln_CN_ratio", "ln_CP_ratio")

for (trait in nutrients) {
  print(
    ggplot(aus_data, aes(x = .data[[trait]])) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~ myc_type, scales = "free") +
  theme_classic()
  )
  
  print(
    ggplot(aus_data, aes(sample = .data[[trait]])) +
      stat_qq(distribution = stats::qnorm) +
      stat_qq_line(colour = "red", distribution = stats::qnorm ) +
      facet_wrap(~ myc_type, scales = "free") +
      theme_classic() +
      labs(title = paste("Q-Q plots:", trait))
  )
}
```

Despite sample missingness causing extremely non-normal distributions,

### ln_leaf_N

Plot for diagnostic residuals.

```{r}
myc_aov_N <- aov(ln_leaf_N ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(myc_aov_N)

aggregate(ln_leaf_N ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, mean)
```

EcM and EcM-AM have essentially the same means, which isn't surprising. AM and NM-AM are also quite similar.

```{r}
#test assumption of normality of residuals
hist(resid(myc_aov_N))

#look at distribution per level
ggplot(aus_data, aes(x = ln_leaf_N)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~ myc_type, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()

#look at normality per level
myc_types <- na.omit(unique(aus_data$myc_type))
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))

for (myc in myc_types) {
  x <- filter(aus_data, myc_type == myc)$ln_leaf_N
  qqnorm(x, main = myc)
  qqline(x, col = "red")
}

#test assumption of homogeneity of variance
bartlett.test(ln_leaf_N ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)
library(car)
leveneTest(ln_leaf_N ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)

#check how much variance varies among groups
aggregate(ln_leaf_N ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, sd)
```

Residuals look normal enough. Substantial deviation of normality within each level, but qqplots look somewhat acceptable. Bartlett test and levene test passed, so null hypothesis of homogenous variance rejected. EcM and ErM vary little relative to the others, which makes sense given they have the smallest sample size.

Do Welch's ANOVA:

```{r}
myc_aov_welch_N <- oneway.test(ln_leaf_N ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, var.equal = FALSE)
myc_aov_welch_N

test_results <- myc_aov_welch_N %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  mutate(test_source = "myctype_leaf_N") %>% 
  bind_rows(test_results, . )
```

Post-hoc test: Can't use tukey since assumption of equal variances is not met.

```{r}
library(rstatix)
posthoc_myc_leafN <- games_howell_test(aus_data, ln_leaf_N ~ myc_type)
posthoc_myc_leafN
```

As expected, only non-significant contrasts from AM and NM-AM, and EcM and EcM-AM.

### ln_leaf_P

Plot diagnostic residuals. Not yet decided on final model.

```{r}

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

aggregate(ln_leaf_P ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, mean)
```

Each individual category has distinctive means. Variances appear more homogenous than leaf N.

```{r}

#look at distribution per level
```

Do Welch's ANOVA:

```{r}
myc_aov_welch_P <- oneway.test(ln_leaf_P ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, var.equal = FALSE)
myc_aov_welch_P

test_results <- myc_aov_welch_P %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  mutate(test_source = "myctype_leaf_P") %>% 
  bind_rows(test_results, . )
```

Post-hoc test: Can't use tukey since assumption of equal variances is not met.

```{r}
posthoc_myc_leafP <- games_howell_test(aus_data, ln_leaf_P ~ myc_type)
posthoc_myc_leafP
```

Non-significant contrasts from EcM and ErM mostly.

```{r}

#look at distribution per level
ggplot(aus_data, aes(x = leaf_C_per_dry_mass)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~ myc_type, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()

#look at normality per level
myc_types <- na.omit(unique(aus_data$myc_type))

bartlett.test(leaf_C_per_dry_mass ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)
```

Residuals extremely non-normal distributions within some levels, particularly the low sample sizes - will make the assumption from the qqlines that they would approximate a normal dist if we had more values. Extremely uneven variances as well, but likely due to uneven sample sizes as well.

Do Welch's ANOVA:

```{r}
myc_aov_welch_C <- oneway.test(leaf_C_per_dry_mass ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, var.equal = FALSE)
myc_aov_welch_C

test_results <- myc_aov_welch_C %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  mutate(test_source = "myctype_leaf_C") %>% 
  bind_rows(test_results, . )
```

Post-hoc test: Can't use tukey since assumption of equal variances is not met.

```{r}
posthoc_myc_leafC <- games_howell_test(aus_data, leaf_C_per_dry_mass ~ myc_type)
posthoc_myc_leafC
```

Non-significant contrasts from EcM and ErM mostly.

### ln_NP_ratio

Plot diagnostic residuals. Not yet decided on final model.

```{r}
myc_aov_NP <- aov(ln_NP_ratio ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(myc_aov_NP)

aggregate(ln_NP_ratio ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, mean)
```

EcM-AM, NM, and NM_AM have similar means. AM has notably different means. Variances appear more homogenous than leaf N. Color residuals by mycorrhizal type:

```{r}
#test assumption of normality of residuals
hist(resid(myc_aov_NP))

#look at distribution per level
ggplot(aus_data, aes(x = ln_NP_ratio)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~ myc_type, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()

#look at normality per level
myc_types <- na.omit(unique(aus_data$myc_type))
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))

for (myc in myc_types) {
  x <- filter(aus_data, myc_type == myc)$ln_NP_ratio
  qqnorm(x, main = myc)
  qqline(x, col = "red")
}

#test assumption of homogeneity of variance
bartlett.test(ln_NP_ratio ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)
library(car)
leveneTest(ln_NP_ratio ~ as.factor(myc_type), data = aus_data)

#check how much variance varies among groups
aggregate(ln_NP_ratio ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, sd)
```

Substantial deviation of normality within each level, especially ErM, but qqplots look somewhat acceptable. Bartlett test and levene test passed, so null hypothesis of homogenous variance rejected. ErM varies more than other categories notably.

Do Welch's ANOVA:

```{r}
myc_aov_welch_NP <- oneway.test(ln_NP_ratio ~ myc_type, data = aus_data, var.equal = FALSE)
myc_aov_welch_NP

test_results <- myc_aov_welch_NP %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  mutate(test_source = "myctype_leaf_NP") %>% 
  bind_rows(test_results, . )
```

Post-hoc test: Can't use tukey since assumption of equal variances is not met.

```{r}
posthoc_myc_leafNP <- games_howell_test(aus_data, ln_NP_ratio ~ myc_type)
posthoc_myc_leafNP
```

Non-significant contrasts spread across the categories.

This is code for the question: does membership of each individual mycorrhizal type lead to higher or lower leaf nitrogen, whilst accounting for the other mycorrhizal types? It is not "is there a difference in the means between these mycorhizzal types?"

```{r}
library(emmeans)
#check assumption of equal variance
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(filter(aus_data, AM ==1)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N AM")
hist(filter(aus_data, AM ==0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N AM")

hist(filter(aus_data, EcM ==1)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N EcM")
hist(filter(aus_data, EcM ==0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N EcM")

hist(filter(aus_data, NM ==1)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N NM")
hist(filter(aus_data, NM ==0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N NM")

hist(filter(aus_data, ErM ==1)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N ErM")
hist(filter(aus_data, ErM ==0)$ln_leaf_N, main = "leaf N ErM")

#var.test(ln_leaf_N ~ AM + EcM + NM + ErM, data = aus_data) 
#bartlett.test(ln_leaf_N ~ AM + EcM + NM + ErM, data = aus_data)
#leveneTest(ln_leaf_N ~ AM + EcM + NM + ErM, data = aus_data)

#do test
aov_mod <- aov(data = aus_data, ln_leaf_N ~ as.factor(AM) + as.factor(EcM) + as.factor(NM) + as.factor(ErM))
summary(aov_mod)
#check assumption of normality of residuals
plot(aov_mod)
qqnorm(resid(aov_mod))
qqline(resid(aov_mod))
hist(resid(aov_mod))
```

After accounting fo the other associations, AM, EcM, and NM differ in leaf nitrogen between 1 and 0.

Just do an ANOVA and justify it as being independent.

```{r}
myc_colors <- c("red", "blue", "green", "orange", "purple", "brown")

# Get the observations actually used by the model
model_data <- model.frame(myc_aov_P)

names(model_data)[names(model_data) == "as.factor(myc_type)"] <- "myc_type"

# Generate colours from the model's mycorrhizal types
myc_model <- as.factor(model_data$myc_type)
cols <- myc_colors[myc_model]

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

for (i in c(1, 2, 3, 5)) {
  plot(myc_aov_P, which = i, col = cols)

  legend("topright",
         legend = levels(myc_model),
         col = myc_colors[seq_along(levels(myc_model))],
         pch = 1,
         cex = 0.7)
}
```
